newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU's Bonino says Zaire fighting risks new genocide.
newsitem.headline: EU's Bonino says Zaire fighting risks new genocide.

text.p: European Humanitarian Aid Commissioner Emma Bonino appealed to warring parties in Zaire on Friday to stop fighting or risk seeing further genocide in central Africa's great lakes region.
"A new genocide is possibly in the offing," the European Union's aid chief told a news conference.

Bonino spoke as reports from Bujumbura in Burundi spoke of heavy shelling in the east Zairean town of Uvira overnight and on Friday, the latest fighting between the Zairean army and Banyamulenge rebels.
"I believe that we and the international community have to make clear to those who started this military action that the fate of a million people is in their hands," Bonino said.
"The international community must make it clear that it will not tolerate another genocide," she added.

The Commissioner said efforts to feed the 1.2 million refugees spread between three main centres in eastern Zaire faced severe problems because of fighting which had blocked links between Uvira and Bukavu to the north.
She said EU food stocks were sufficient for several weeks' supply, as were supplies held by the World Food Programme, but added that the problem would be in their distribution.
More than 200,000 Rwandan and Burundian refugees have fled camps north of Uvira towards the city of Bukavu in the past week because of fighting.
Aid officials fear the Tutsi rebellion in eastern Zaire could spread further and Tutsi-dominated armies in neighbouring Burundi and Rwanda could join the conflict.
Zairean President Mobutu Sese Seko is in Switzerland, receiving chemotherapy after an operation for cancer in August, fuelling fears the revolt might herald the break-up of Zaire.
